sources.note: Original indexed printed p27: Greek/Roman mudbrick on stone foundations and later reuse. Do not confuse separate English booklet medieval houses with Hellenistic houses.

sources.title: Greshnikov and colleagues, Studies of Composite Protective Coatings of an Ancient Ship from Phanagoria
sources.note: Open full primary study, introduction, discussion and conclusions. Published online 2025, volume dated 2024. Mid-first-century BCE radiocarbon; avoid an exact sinking year or calling the bow fitting an offensive ram.

sources.title: Heinz Heinen, Hypsikrateia / Hypsikrates: a new Greek inscription from Phanagoria
sources.note: Full academic PDF read, printed pp219 to 221. The Greek word χαῖρε is unbracketed; the stonecutter corrected gyne to gynai. Screenshot service failed but indexed original correctly renders Greek and translation; extracted Greek font encoding is faulty. Do not assert death in the revolt as proven.

sources.title: Phanagoria expedition: four inscriptions from underwater excavation
sources.note: Direct original expedition text read: reused harbour stones, Aspurgus and portico restoration of 220 CE. Later evidence explicitly labelled.

sources.title: A. L. Yermolin, Center and Periphery in Late Antiquity: Bosporus
sources.note: Author-uploaded full academic article read, Tractus Aevorum 7(2), 2020, pp180 to 181. Used only for persistence beyond cessation of coinage and early sixth-century Byzantine incorporation, not its stronger uniform destruction claims.

sources.note: Original indexed full summary read; direct opening errors. Master of Macedon from316, royal title about305, death297. Use these over tourism page inconsistent316 to 298 reign label.

sources.note: Official history directly indexed: foundation316/5, Cassandreia, wife and relocation26townships. Its Roman province shortcut is not used.

sources.title: Hellenic Ministry of Culture, Cultural Egnatia: Pella
sources.note: Direct full page read. Urban plan, clay pipes/cleaning access, courtyard homes and late-fourth-century mosaics. Hellenistic infrastructure not all dated exactly to Cassander. Source budget must be shared if later Macedon card uses same URL.

sources.title: Ephorate of Antiquities of Pella: international conference abstracts, 2023
sources.note: Direct full PDF. Swimming pool/dressing room/bath dated late fourth century from ceramics and Alexander/Cassander bronze coins. Royal use only.

sources.title: Ephorate of Antiquities of Pella: Archaeological Museum of Pella

sources.title: University of Canterbury and Otago Museum: Alexanders under his successors
sources.note: Direct catalogue figure10, Otago Museum OM403 bronze coin, circa305 to 297BCE, inscription with translation. Denomination drachm probably mistaken for bronze; do not repeat.

sources.note: Full primary-text edition and English translation, pp204 to 205.306 to 297BCE inscription, earlier decision likely316; now lost stone known from older records. Shared source budget reserved for Lysimachus no5; this module uses under110words.

batchIdentityNotes.note: world-bc323, bc300 and bc100 share a broad footprint, bbox 33.3957,44.4916,40.3186,48.7759; imported coverage -323 to -1. Core Kerch/Taman political identity is clear, northern extent not precise. Public caveat supplied. No alias to Pontic kingdom; Mithridates material identifies his period of control. Medieval Phanagoria parasite and household evidence excluded.

world-bc300 bbox19.3376,38.3479,24.9320,42.5368; imported -300 to -200. Clearly Macedonian/Greek kingdom, not modern NorthMacedonia. Public overview and ending explicitly correct the overlong interval. No alias to macedon-and-hellenic-league because distinct ruler and era. Pella material is explicitly late-fourth-century or broadly Hellenistic, never all personally commissioned by Cassander.
